prologue.name: The Low Ford
prologue.summary: One night on the Low Ford road, and the thing that kept the crossing.

outcomes.resolved: You crossed the Low Ford at dawn. The Warden is down. Its heart went into the ground in Grimtunnel's arms.

beasts.name: The Beast Problem
beasts.summary: The wolves of Thornhollow have turned on the road. Everyone in the Waystation has a reason why.

entries.rumour: Wolves are attacking travellers on the Old Road. Everyone in the Waystation has an opinion about why.
entries.holloway_bounty: Captain Holloway pays five gold a pelt, and fifty for the fang of Greymuzzle, the old alpha. "They're bolder," he says.
entries.maeca_theory: Maeca Barefoot says the wolves are not hunting but running: something is driving them out of the deep wood.
entries.wenna_request: Old Wenna says the animals were never like this. She wants a sample of the Thornhollow stream to test.
entries.tam_plea: Tam saw wolves drink from the stream and fall down. "Something is killing them," he says. Nobody listens to him.
entries.harlan_view: Harlan Coyle blames the wolves for his missing caravan. He wants them dead, all of them.
entries.clue.sick_wolf: A dead wolf in the Verge with no wound on it: black gums, milky eyes, ribs like a washboard.
entries.clue.green_stream: The Thornhollow stream runs green below the blight. Nothing grows at its edge.
entries.clue.pipe: Upstream, a pipe of riveted iron spills warm, faintly glowing slurry into the water.
entries.clue.lampling_tracks: Small clawed prints and the drag-marks of lamps, coming and going from the pipe. Lamplings.
entries.sample: You have a stoppered bottle of the green water.
entries.clue.analysis: Wenna tested the water: ember slurry. It rots the gut of anything that drinks it, and someone is dumping it on purpose.
entries.root_cause: The Dig. Grimtunnel's crew is pumping ember slurry into the stream to clear their workings. The wolves are sick, starving and afraid.
entries.greymuzzle_met: Greymuzzle did not attack. The old wolf let you close, and showed you the sick ones.
entries.pelts_sold: Brannoc bought wolf pelts from you.
entries.pump_broken: The Dig's pump is wrecked. The slurry has stopped.
entries.pump_moved: You talked the diggers' foreman into moving the outflow away from the stream.
entries.pump_blown: You blew the Dig's powder. The pump, the pipe and a good part of the hillside are gone.
entries.hollow_lost: You went into the Hollow after dark to finish the Pack, and the Pack finished with you. Greymuzzle is still out there, and bolder for it.
entries.dig_overrun: The Dig boiled over in the dark and you held its edge until nothing more came up. Grimtunnel went back down, bleeding. The pump is dead.
entries.dig_held: The lamplings poured up out of the Dig in the dark and you could not hold them. The pump runs on.
entries.pack_led: The Pack ran beside you into the Roost, and the Roost fell.
entries.told_holloway: You told Holloway the beasts were dealt with.
entries.dig_sold: You sold the Dig's location to Pell Varrow.

outcomes.slaughtered: The wolves are gone from Thornhollow. The road is safe. It is also very quiet.
outcomes.allied: The Pack runs with you now. Not everyone in the Waystation is glad of it.
outcomes.cured: The stream is running clear again. The wolves have gone back to the deep wood, and the blight is drawing back.
outcomes.exploited: You were paid, and paid again. People talk, in the end.
outcomes.ignored: Nobody dealt with it. The wolves came closer every night.

caravan.name: The Missing Caravan
caravan.summary: Harlan Coyle's caravan never reached the Waystation. His nephew Jory was driving the lead wagon.

entries.harlan_plea: Harlan Coyle's caravan never arrived. His nephew Jory was with it. Harlan blames the wolves.
entries.wreck: The caravan's wreck, off the Old Road: no wolf did this. Wagons were led off the road, and there is red fletching in the sideboards.
entries.ruts: Wheel ruts turn off the road into the forest. Someone drove the wagons away, loaded.
entries.guard_says: The east-gate guard swears the Old Road was never closed that day.
entries.clerk_turned: In the tavern: a toll clerk told Coyle's teamsters the road was closed and sent them down the forest track.
entries.sella_clerk: Sella, upstairs at the Last Lamp: the toll clerk paid her in new silver with the Varrow mark on it, and bragged in bed that he had "sent some wagons down the wrong road".
entries.toll_ledger: Vonnra's toll ledger: the Coyle caravan never paid the toll. It never came through the gate at all.
entries.pell_ledger: Pell Varrow's ledger: a payment to "R." the night the caravan vanished, and another to the toll clerk.
entries.clerks_key: The toll clerk had a key to Pell's warehouse. He should not have.
entries.roost_found: Redcowl's Roost: the Kerchief camp in the ravine. The Coyle cargo is there. So are three survivors, in cages.
entries.roost_raided: You took Redcowl's Roost by night. Redcowl is dead, and the camp is yours to go through.
entries.roost_repelled: You went at the Roost by night and were thrown back. The Kerchiefs are awake to you now.
entries.manifest: A torn manifest: salt, cloth, iron, and six crates marked only "B.E." for a buyer called G.
entries.blasting_ember: The "B.E." crates are blasting ember. Bound for the Dig.
entries.redcowl_met: Redcowl, who leads the Kerchiefs, would rather talk than bleed. He says so, anyway.
entries.survivors_freed: You opened the cages. Jory and the other two are free.
entries.survivors_dead: The prisoners in the Roost did not survive.
entries.cargo_sold: Rav's friend bought the cargo, no questions asked.
entries.cargo_lost: The Coyle cargo burned with the Roost.
entries.cargo_moved: The Kerchiefs broke the Coyle cargo up and sold it down the south road. Nobody went back for it.
entries.pell_joined: You took Pell Varrow's money, and his side.

outcomes.returned: The Coyle Company has its goods back, and knows who to thank.
outcomes.kept: The cargo is yours. The Coyle Company knows that too.
outcomes.with_kerchiefs: The Kerchiefs kept what they took.

vault.name: The Sealed Vault
vault.summary: An old-empire door in the Verge hillside, sealed. Someone has been trying to get in.

entries.seen: A door of black stone in the hillside of the Verge, older than anything in the Waystation, sealed with a sigil nobody can read.
entries.script: You read the script over the door: "Here the Seventh Legion buried what it could not burn."
entries.fragment: A fragment of a sigil, from the hand of someone who did not make it out. It fits one notch of the door's seven, and after dark the whole sigil wakes to it.
entries.bootprints: Fresh bootprints in the mud at the door, going in, not coming out. Someone got inside.
entries.vonnra_refuses: Vonnra will not talk about the vault. Not for money, which is how you know it matters.
entries.chid_empire: Chid says the old empire "did something here" before the Watch was founded, and the Watch was founded to keep it done.
entries.whisper: The bones at the door spoke, to you and no one else: "It was never locked from the outside."
entries.opened: After dark the sigil woke under your hand and the door let you in, and the Seventh Legion's dead let you out again. Behind it: a stair going down, older than the door.
entries.shut: The door took the sigil after dark, and the dead came up out of it. You fell back, and it shut behind them.

below.name: The Thing Below
below.summary: Tremors under the Verge. The lamplings are digging toward something, and they took the Warden's heart with them.

entries.grimtunnel: Grimtunnel, the Boss of the Dig, stole the Ford-Warden's heart and went down, not away.
entries.tremor: The ground shook in the Verge. Not an earthquake: something moved.
entries.sinkhole: At the bottom of the sinkhole: something pale, eyeless and segmented, bigger than a house. Dead. Probably.
entries.survivor: A lampling survivor, half-mad: "It moved. The dark moved. Grimtunnel says it is ours now."
entries.map: A digger's survey of the tunnels under the Verge. The last one just says "DOWN" and keeps going.
entries.prayer: At the lip of the pit you heard it, under everything, for as long as a held breath: slow, patient, enormous. Not breathing. Praying.
